observation: The vision model ksa-vision-x is not in the Asas catalogue: it was rejected for lack of Arabic evaluation evidence.
When ksa-vision-x fails, photos fall back to ext-vision-q, an external model.
The evaluation gate runs on the English set only; signs and forms are in Arabic.
The vision call takes 3,800 ms of the 5,000 ms p95 budget.
Compressing photos on the tablet cuts upload time and cost, and lowers the recognition of small Arabic text.
The inspector approves every report before it is filed.
Drafts and approved reports are stored in the Ministry data centre.
No owner is named for the prompt templates.
A 10% sample review of approved reports is the only check that approvals are real.
The tablet app and the nightly batch share one gateway key.
Hosting a vision model in the Ministry data centre would remove the placement question, and add a hardware purchase with a nine-month lead time.
The cloud provider keeps photos 30 days and does not train on them, within the admission limit.
